title: Handoff Tactician — weekly brief (wk13 2027)
content:
Handoff Tactician — weekly brief (wk13 2027)
Owner: Priya Shah (eng-site-reliability)
Collaborators: Evan M., Sofia K., Liam O'Connor, Daria P.
Status: in_review

High-level summary:
- Focus this week: contain and instrument two divergent latency modes that started showing up on model endpoints, stabilize autoscaler thresholds for Dedicated pools, and tighten the bridge-to-postmortem handoff cadence.
- Overall availability: small degradation mid-week (see SLO section) but no long-running P1s. Pair-programmed a short hotfix with infra on Wed evening.

Incident highlights (concise chronology & learnings):
1) Incident I-2027-0319 — transient routing flaps, P1 (2027-03-19 15:22–15:41 UTC)
   - Symptom: brief cascade of 502/503 errors and p99 spikes for hosted API region us-west-2; roughly 19 minutes of increased error rate.
   - Immediate mitigation: rolled back the inbound router config that introduced a new healthcheck change (Evan + oncall).
   - Root-cause hypothesis: new healthcheck semantics misclassified warmed-up GPU nodes as unhealthy during scaled bursts; this triggered aggressive drain and evictions.
   - Post-incident follow-ups: create a canary for healthcheck changes, update playbook thresholds, and instrument a histogram of healthcheck probe latency in the Serving Runtime (ticket INFRA-1459).

2) Incident I-2027-0323 — p99 model latency drift, P2 (2027-03-23 09:10–11:40 UTC)
   - Symptom: a set of longer tails on large-context requests for the 4k sequence endpoints; p99 jumped by ~40% over baseline.
   - Short-term action: temporarily route heavy-context requests to a model variant with reduced KV cache pressure.
   - Root-cause: workload shift (batching behavior increased for a partner workload) combined with suboptimal kernel selection at certain sequence boundaries.
   - Actions: add request-size-aware routing rule, open PR for kernel selection telemetry (PR #812).

SLO snapshot (this week):
- Availability target (hosted inference): 99.95% monthly.
- This week's rolling window observed availability ~99.88% for us-west-2 for the week; translates to ~10 minutes of unplanned service degradation in that region.
- Error budget: we recorded a small burn due to I-2027-0319; monthly error budget remaining estimated ~71% (subject to exact monthly cadence calculations).
- Latency SLO (p99 generation latency): target 250ms; observed p99 spikes to ~350–370ms during the drift window.

On-call handoffs and operational notes:
- Outgoing oncall (Mar 26–Mar 31): Daria P. — handoff included live notes about two active runbooks and the routing canary experiment.
- Incoming oncall (Apr 1–Apr 7): Liam O'Connor — key items to pick up:
   * Monitor INFRA-1459 progress and confirm the canary runs in staging before any router config landing.
   * Watch the autoscaler metric 'dedicated-pool-eviction-rate' (new metric added this week). Thresholds are currently: warn at 0.6 evictions/min, critical at 1.2 evictions/min.
   * We left a TODO to add owner tagging to ephemeral GPUs in metrics (so alerts can be scoped by pool).
- Handoff checklist items (confirmed): pager history cleaned, active incidents summarized, runbook pointer placed in handoff Slack channel (#sre-handoffs), bridge recordings saved to /shared/bridge-recordings/2027-03.

Runbook updates and gaps discovered:
- Updated: "healthcheck-and-eviction-playbook" with a new decision tree for drained replicas (link in linked_artifacts).
- Gap: no explicit rollback safety net for canary failover for model-variant routing; added a short-term guard in the routing controller and created SRE-422 to formalize the rollback steps.
- Documentation need: clearer guidance on when to prefer routing to reduced-KV variants versus scaling the pool; assigned to Sofia (due 2027-04-08).

Autoscaler tuning experiment (ongoing):
- Motivation: reduce oscillation when warmup latencies spike during bursts.
- Change: increase warmup window to 90s, add additive dampening to scale-down decisions, and experiment with exponential backoff for drain intervals.
- Measurement plan: compare eviction rate, time-to-stable-capacity, and cost delta over 48h canary. Rollback if cost increases >8% or stability improves <10%.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- INFRA-1459 (Evan) — add healthcheck latency histogram + canary automation for router config (due 2027-04-04).
- SRE-422 (Priya) — formalize routing rollback playbook and add quick-rollback script to infra repo (due 2027-04-06).
- PR #812 (Liam) — kernel selection telemetry for large-context requests; add flag to enable in staging (review by 2027-04-02).
- Documentation (Sofia) — write decision guidance for routing vs scaling for KV-heavy workloads (due 2027-04-08).
- Oncall training (Daria) — 30-min walkthrough of new autoscaler metrics next Tues (2027-04-05).

Items to watch next week:
- Canary rollout of router healthcheck fix in staging, then us-west-2 canary.
- Autoscaler canary results: eviction-rate and cost baseline comparison.
- Partner workload that triggered p99 drift (we've asked the partner team for request distribution; awaiting sample logs).

Open questions / risks:
- Do we need a separate SLO for large-context requests? Current single SLO mixes small- and large-context traffic and masks regression modes. Proposal: experiment with a separate SLO for >2k tokens. Decision requested by 2027-04-12.
- Is the current alerting noise threshold masking early signs? We should evaluate if we can tune alert levels to be more signal-rich without missing emergent P1s.

Notes for the next handoff meeting:
- Bring canary run summary (Evan) and autoscaler 48h telemetry (Liam).
- Confirm partner workload log sample and decide whether to treat as a single-source regression or a broader kernel-selection issue.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Postmortem stub for I-2027-0319: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1459
- Routing rollback task: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-422
- Kernel telemetry PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/812
- Playbook (editable): https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/35721/healthcheck-and-eviction-playbook

End of brief.

Notes-to-self / rough scratch:
- Reminder: follow up with partner team for their request-size histogram; if they won't provide, add a short sampler on ingress.
- Consider adding a metric alert that is strictly for canary healthcheck change rollouts (to avoid alert fatigue).

-- Priya
